newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LATE OWN GOALS CHANGE COURSE OF F.A. CUP MATCHES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LATE OWN GOALS CHANGE COURSE OF F.A. CUP MATCHES.

text.p: Two own goals changed the course of the F.A. Cup on Sunday with one handing Sheffield Wednesday a win at Bradford City and the other giving Leicester City a late equaliser in a 2-2 draw against Chelsea.

Sheffield Wednesday, who last reached the final in 1993 when they lost to Arsenal, stayed on course for Wembley when Nicky Mohan deflected an 84th minute shot from Ritchie Humphries into his own net for the only goal of the game.

Chelsea, who led 2-0 Leicester at halftime, looked set for a place in the quarterfinals for the fourth time in six seasons, and were still leading Leicester 2-1 with two minutes to go. But Eddie Newton deflected a Garry Parker freekick past his goalkeeper Kevin Hitchock to give Leicester a draw with just two minutes to play.

Goals from Italian Roberto di Matteo after 16 minutes and Mark Hughes after 35 put Chelsea ahead but Steve Walsh gave Leicester -- missing six key players through injury or suspension -- renewed hope with a 52nd minute header.
The match was marred though by scenes of hooliganism which have rarely seen on English grounds since the dark days of the 1980s.
About 100 Chelsea fans fought with Leicester supporters before the kickoff and shortly after the match started. Police made a number of arrests and at least one crowd steward was hurt in the melee.
Saturday's results produced three shock results which saw the elimination of two premier league teams and one from the first division.

The biggest surprise was second division Chesterfield's 1-0 win over Nottingham Forest to put them into the quarter-finals for the first time in their 106-year history, while first division Portsmouth stunned Leeds 3-2 at Elland Road and second division Wrexham knocked out first division Birmingham 3-1.

One fifth round tie is still to be played. The all-premier league match between Derby and Coventry is set for February 26 following Coventry's 2-1 win over Blackburn in a fourth round match on Saturday.
